Owners of an **independent upper-upscale hotel** usually begin with the major **soft brands or collection brands**, because these preserve much of the property’s name, design and identity while adding a global reservation system and loyalty program.

### Most commonly considered

| Parent company | Brand | Typical positioning / fit |
|---|---|---|
| **Marriott** | **Autograph Collection** | Often a leading candidate for distinctive, design-forward upper-upscale or luxury hotels with strong local character. |
| **Marriott** | **Tribute Portfolio** | Generally suited to independent upper-upscale lifestyle hotels seeking somewhat more flexibility than a traditional hard brand. Marriott specifically positions Autograph, Tribute and Luxury Collection as operating models for independent hotels. ([hotel-development.marriott.com](https://www.hotel-development.marriott.com/brands/premium-brands?utm_source=openai)) |
| **Hilton** | **Curio Collection by Hilton** | Hilton’s principal collection option for high-end, full-service independent hotels with distinctive architecture, food and beverage, and locally driven experiences. ([stories.hilton.com](https://stories.hilton.com/curio-collection-by-hilton-fact-sheet?utm_source=openai)) |
| **Hyatt** | **The Unbound Collection by Hyatt** | Upper-upscale/luxury, story-driven properties—particularly landmark urban hotels and distinctive resorts. ([hyatt.com](https://www.hyatt.com/development/ourbrands/theunboundcollectionbyhyatt?utm_source=openai)) |
| **Hyatt** | **JdV by Hyatt** | More lifestyle-oriented and typically smaller or neighborhood-focused than Unbound, but still classified by Hyatt as upper-upscale. ([hyatt.com](https://www.hyatt.com/development/ourbrands?utm_source=openai)) |
| **IHG** | **Vignette Collection** | Primarily luxury, but frequently evaluated for top-end upper-upscale conversions where the hotel wants to retain its existing name, look and feel. ([development.ihg.com](https://development.ihg.com/hotel-brands/vignette-collection?utm_source=openai)) |
| **Accor** | **MGallery Collection** | Accor’s upper-upscale boutique collection, aimed at hotels with a strong individual story and design identity. ([group.accor.com](https://group.accor.com/en/news-stories/collection-brands-handwritten-emblems-mgallery?utm_source=openai)) |
| **Choice/Radisson** | **Radisson Individuals** | Positioned in the Americas as an upper-upscale soft brand for full-service boutique and independent hotels. ([choicehotelsdevelopment.com](https://www.choicehotelsdevelopment.com/news/choice-hotels-relaunches-radisson-individuals-as-part-of-its-portfolio-of-brands-MCGUOTHASSNZBF5OUH7E7UATMTII?utm_source=openai)) |

### Other conversion alternatives

Depending on product quality, renovation budget and target rate:

- **Tapestry Collection by Hilton** — normally a step below Curio, but worth considering if the property is closer to upscale than true upper-upscale. ([stories.hilton.com](https://stories.hilton.com/releases/hiltons-curio-and-tapestry-collections-celebrate-200th-hotel-milestones?utm_source=openai))
- **voco by IHG** — an explicitly conversion-oriented upscale/premium brand with relatively flexible standards and potentially lower capital requirements; unlike a pure collection brand, the hotel generally takes the voco identity. ([development.ihg.com](https://development.ihg.com/hotel-brands/voco-hotels?utm_source=openai))
- **Ascend Hotel Collection** — flexible and conversion-friendly, but generally positioned as upscale rather than upper-upscale. ([choicehotelsdevelopment.com](https://www.choicehotelsdevelopment.com/sfsites/c/cms/delivery/media/MCUMJCKAM4XNGDBGYQ36NVQN55WE?utm_source=openai))
- **Luxury Collection, LXR Hotels & Resorts, Emblems Collection or Vignette Collection** — possible if the property can credibly reach luxury service, design and capital standards.
- Traditional “hard-brand” conversions such as **Renaissance, Le Méridien, Hilton, Hyatt Regency, Kimpton, Hotel Indigo or Crowne Plaza** may also be evaluated when preserving the independent identity is less important.

In a typical U.S. owner-selection process, the core competitive set would usually be **Autograph, Tribute, Curio, Unbound and Radisson Individuals**, with **MGallery or Vignette** added where Accor or IHG distribution is compelling. The ultimate shortlist depends heavily on market availability and territorial protection, required property-improvement-plan spending, franchise fees, loyalty contribution, group demand, food-and-beverage requirements and the amount of operational independence the owner wants to retain.
